simple.meaning: הֲלֹם (hălôm) is a Hebrew object word meaning “hither.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 16:13. The surrounding context includes Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֲלֹם (H1988) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: הֲלֹם (hălôm) / H1988 is traced through Genesis 16:13, Exodus 3:5, Judges 18:3, Judges 20:7 with generated occurrence evidence.

firstOccurrence.englishText: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”

timeline.evidenceText: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”
He said, “Don’t come close. Take off your sandals, for the place you are standing on is holy ground.”

When they were by the house of Micah, they knew the voice of the young man the Levite; so they went over there and said to him, “Who brought you here? What do you do in this place? What do you have here?”
Behold, you children of Israel, all of you, give here your advice and counsel.”
At meal time Boaz said to her, “Come here, and eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar.”
Therefore they asked of Yahweh further, “Is there yet a man to come here?”
Saul said, “Let’s go down after the Philistines by night, and take plunder among them until the morning light, and let’s not leave a man of them.”
Saul said, “Draw near here, all you chiefs of the people; and know and see in which this sin has been today.
Then David the king went in, and sat before Yahweh; and he said, “Who am I, Lord* The word translated “Lord” is “Adonai.” Yahweh, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
Then David the king went in, and sat before Yahweh; and he said, “Who am I, Yahweh God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far?
Therefore their people return to them,

definitions.full: H1988. halom הֲלֹם adverb of place, hither (Arabic hither! ) — Exod 3:5 הֲלֹם אַלתִּֿקְרַב approach not hither , Judg 18:3 ; 20:7 ; 1Sam 10:22 ; 14:16 and lo, the camp melted away וַהֲלֹם וַיֵּלֶךְ read with ᵐ5 ( ἔνθεν καὶ ἔνθεν ) Th We Dr וַהֲלֹם הֲלֹם hither and thither i.e. in different directions (compare וָהֵנָּה הֵנָּה Josh 8:20 ), Joshua 8:36; Joshua 8:38; Ruth 2:14 ; הֲלֹם עַד figurative hitherto, thus far (i.e. to this point of dignity and greatness) 2Sam 7:18 (= 1Chr 17:16 ). Psa 73:10 , if text be sound, הֲלֹם must mean thither (that is, after the persons described 73:3 ); but such sense questionable; read probably with Houb La for לָ֑חֶם יַשְׂבִּעֵמוֺ הלם, עמו ישיב satisfies them with bread: compare Che Hup Now. Gen 16:13 = here ; but here also text is dubious: v Di. Judg 14:15 read הֲלֹם for הֲלֹא : see הֲ 1 end .
